The code in these notes, and in the homework, is Python with PyTorch [@paszke2019pytorch],
plus NumPy where a lecture builds a method from scratch.
Every example here runs in seconds on a laptop's CPU;
the homework trains larger models.

These notes build on [lds](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/), the notes for DATA 371/471,
and link to its definitions rather than repeating them.
Its chapters on
[gradient descent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html),
[logistic regression](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/logistic-regression.html),
[neural networks](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html)
and [backpropagation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/backpropagation.html)
are the ones these notes lean on most.
